hook: The Virgin Queen who beat the Armada and gave her name to a golden age.

pages.x: Elizabeth was born in 1533, the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. When she was two, her father had her mother beheaded and declared Elizabeth illegitimate. She grew up clever, learning Latin, Greek, French and Italian.
pages.cap: Hatfield House, where she grew up

pages.x: When her Catholic half-sister Mary became queen, Elizabeth was suspected of a Protestant plot and taken to the Tower of London by the Traitors' Gate. She expected to be executed, like her mother.

Mary died in 1558, and Elizabeth became queen at 25. She made England Protestant again, but tried not to persecute Catholics for their private beliefs. She had no wish, she said, to "make windows into men's souls".
She never married, though kings and princes courted her for years. She said she was married to England. Her favourite, Robert Dudley, caused a scandal. The colony of Virginia was named after her.

Her Catholic cousin Mary, Queen of Scots, fled to England in 1568. Plotters wanted to put Mary on Elizabeth's throne. After 19 years of captivity and plots, Elizabeth signed Mary's death warrant in 1587.

In 1588 the Spanish Armada sailed. Elizabeth rode out to her troops at Tilbury: "I know I have the body of a weak and feeble woman; but I have the heart and stomach of a king." English fireships and storms scattered the Armada.

Her reign saw Shakespeare's plays, Drake's voyage around the world and the first English colonies in America. She whitened her face with lead paint to hide smallpox scars. She died in 1603, the last of the Tudors.
Elizabeth ruled for 44 years and gave her name to a golden age. She kept England Protestant and independent, and her speech at Tilbury is still quoted.
pts: Ruled in the golden age of Shakespeare
